exercises.why: **нёс** — нести́ (imperfective): to bear, to bring, to carry; to carry, to bear, to support; to lay (eggs); (colloquial, pejorative) to talk (about), to babble on (about).
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **носи** — носи́ть (imperfective): to carry, to bear (a burden); (of wind, water, etc.) to carry along, to drive; to have something (e.g. a name, sideburns, a gun...); to wear (clothes, shoes or makeup).
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **произнёс** — произнести́ (perfective): to pronounce, to articulate; to deliver, to utter. Wiktionary: про- + изнести́.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: отноше́ние — attitude; носи́ть — to carry, to bear (a burden); произнести́ — to pronounce, to articulate; приноси́ть — to bring (by foot), to fetch.

exercises.q: It was me that took out the garbage.
exercises.why: **вынес** — вы́нести (perfective): to carry out, to take out, to bring out, to remove; to transfer; to get, to acquire; to submit. Wiktionary: вы́- + нести́.

exercises.why: **нёсся** — нести́сь (imperfective): to hurtle, to dash, to race, to tear, to scurry (to move rapidly, violently, or without control); to come, (sound) to reach one's ears, to be heard; to lay eggs. Wiktionary: нести́ + -сь.
